obligations.summary: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation, and supervision of AI regulatory sandboxes, covering eligibility criteria, procedures, and terms for participants, in accordance with the examination procedure in Article 98(2).

Implementing acts must ensure AI regulatory sandboxes are open to any applying provider or prospective provider meeting transparent and fair eligibility criteria, and that national competent authorities inform applicants of their decision within three months of application.

Implementing acts must ensure AI regulatory sandboxes allow broad and equal access, keep up with demand for participation, and permit providers and prospective providers to submit applications in partnerships with deployers and other relevant third parties.
Implementing acts must ensure detailed arrangements support flexibility for national competent authorities to establish and operate their AI regulatory sandboxes.

Implementing acts must ensure access to AI regulatory sandboxes is free of charge for SMEs, including start-ups, without prejudice to exceptional costs that national competent authorities may recover in a fair and proportionate manner.
exceptions: National competent authorities may recover exceptional costs in a fair and proportionate manner.

obligations.summary: Implementing acts must ensure AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate providers and prospective providers in complying with conformity assessment obligations and the voluntary application of codes of conduct by means of learning outcomes from the sandboxes.

Implementing acts must ensure AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate involvement of other relevant actors within the AI ecosystem, including notified bodies, standardisation organisations, SMEs, start-ups, researchers, and European Digital Innovation Hubs, to allow cooperation with public and private sectors.

Implementing acts must ensure that procedures and administrative requirements for AI regulatory sandboxes are simple, clearly communicated, and streamlined across the Union to avoid fragmentation, and that participation recognised in one Member State or by the European Data Protection Supervisor carries the same legal effects across the Union.

Implementing acts must ensure that participation in an AI regulatory sandbox is limited to an appropriate period relative to the complexity and scale of the project, with the possibility of extension by the national competent authority.
exceptions: National competent authorities may extend the participation period.

obligations.summary: Implementing acts must ensure AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate development of tools and infrastructure for testing, benchmarking, assessing, and explaining AI system dimensions relevant for regulatory learning, including accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity, and measures to mitigate risks to fundamental rights and society.

National competent authorities shall direct prospective providers in AI regulatory sandboxes, particularly SMEs and start-ups, to pre-deployment services such as regulatory guidance, standardisation and certification support, testing facilities, and European Digital Innovation Hubs where relevant.

Where national competent authorities authorise real-world condition testing within an AI regulatory sandbox, they shall agree specific terms and conditions, including appropriate safeguards to protect fundamental rights, health, and safety with participants, and cooperate with other national competent authorities where appropriate to ensure consistent practices across the Union.
